correctness.rationale: The maximum-simple-path criterion is proved from the maximum-part-size scheduling lemma. At dimensions above t-2 every simplex lies in exactly one contractible class cone, so the relative chain complex splits. Its sole relative group injects into top homology of the simplex skeleton through disjoint supports, proving vanishing outside degree t-2. The image lattice is primitive, so integer homology is torsion-free. Skeletal connectivity plus the homological Whitehead theorem gives the wedge decomposition. Truncated Euler arithmetic gives the closed rank; Hopf--Lefschetz trace on invariant oriented simplices gives the full permutation character. Direct independent small-case forbidden-path enumeration and mod-2 chain ranks passed 67 cases; direct signed fixed-face versus polynomial characters passed 1008 comparisons. Finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The directly closest 2026 primary work supplies the multipartite face decomposition and, in its available abstract, reports complete homotopy classification only for the bipartite case. The new claim treats all numbers of parts >=3 and thresholds >=5, computes the entire nonequivariant integral homotopy type, proves a saturated integral symmetry quotient and evaluates the rational character for every class-preserving permutation. Exact literature/database queries found no equivalent formula or more general homotopy-and-character theorem. The 19-page primary manuscript was not accessible in full, so possible hidden overlap remains an explicit material bibliographic risk.

The parameter-uniform torsion-free sphere-wedge count controls all degrees, the exact integral quotient respects every class-preserving symmetry, and the closed cycle character determines the full rational module for each parameter and conjugacy class. This is not a narrow arbitrary graph example or a recomputation of earlier bipartite special cases. A scholarly downstream use is rational equivariant topology and representation comparison across multipartite parameters. Bibliographic full-text uncertainty is explicit.
